title: Seastone DX010 sai.profile missing SAI_STATS_ST_CAPABILITY_SUPPORTED — syncd segfault (HFTel query) on broadcom-legacy-th 13.2.1 SAI (202605)
author: masteinhauser
body:
### Description

On the `broadcom-legacy-th` SAI (libsaibcm 13.2.1, which carries Tomahawk-1), syncd **segfaults
in `libsai.so.1.0`** during orchagent init on 202605, because the Seastone DX010 sai.profile is
missing the `SAI_STATS_ST_CAPABILITY_SUPPORTED` guard that the Tomahawk-1 reference platform
(Arista 7060CX-32S) already carries.

202605 orchagent (`HFTelOrch::isSupportedHFTel`) **unconditionally** calls
`sai_query_stats_st_capability(..., SAI_OBJECT_TYPE_PORT, ...)` at init (a SAI 1.14 / High-Frequency
Telemetry API). The 13.2.1 SAI predates SAI 1.14 and **null-derefs** on that query instead of
returning `SAI_STATUS_NOT_IMPLEMENTED` → syncd dies → swss crash-loop → ports never plumb. There is
no CONFIG_DB / FEATURE knob to gate the call — it is in syncd SAI-init.

sairedis (`VendorSai::apiInitialize`) reads `SAI_STATS_ST_CAPABILITY_SUPPORTED` from the sai.profile
and, when it is **`0`**, skips the query (returns NOT_IMPLEMENTED), so orchagent's existing
"Streaming stats not supported, HFTel disabled" branch fires cleanly and bring-up proceeds.

The Arista 7060CX-32S (TH1 reference) HWSKU sai.profiles carry the guard; the Seastone DX010 ones
(`device/celestica/x86_64-cel_seastone-r0/*/sai.profile`) do **not**.

### Symptom (on hardware)

- Before: syncd `apiInitialize: SAI_STATS_ST_CAPABILITY_SUPPORTED: NULL`, then
  `kernel: syncd[...]: segfault at 18 ... in libsai.so.1.0`, `child /usr/bin/syncd exited status: 139`
  (SIGSEGV), deterministic every boot; orchagent `APPLY_VIEW` then times out → SIGABRT crash-loop.
- After adding the guard: syncd `apiInitialize: SAI_STATS_ST_CAPABILITY_SUPPORTED=0 in sai.profile,
  disabling query_stats_st_capability for this platform`; orchagent `HFTel disabled`;
  `create_switch` succeeds; 32×100G ports plumb; syncd/swss stable; 0 segfaults.

### Proposed fix

Add to the Seastone DX010 HWSKU sai.profile(s) (mirroring the Arista 7060CX-32S TH1 reference):

```
SAI_STATS_ST_CAPABILITY_SUPPORTED=0
SAI_STATS_EXT_SWITCH_SUPPORTED=0
```

`SAI_STATS_EXT_SWITCH_SUPPORTED=0` pre-empts a second TH1 crash on the 13.2.1 SAI:
`sai_get_stats_ext(SAI_OBJECT_TYPE_SWITCH, ...)` during FlexCounter polling.

### Environment

- Branch: **202605**, kernel 6.12.41+deb13, Debian trixie.
- HW: Celestica Seastone DX010 (BCM56960 / Tomahawk-1), `x86_64-cel_seastone-r0`.
- libsaibcm 13.2.1.120 (`SAI_13.2.1_compat_OCP1.18.1`).

### Related

Companion to the `LAZY_BUILD_INSTALLS` BDE omission in #28125 — both are needed to bring up a
Tomahawk-1 (Seastone) on a 202605 ONIE image.

linkedPullRequests.title: [platform/broadcom]: Fix Tomahawk-1 ONIE image bring-up by adding BDE modules and SAI_STATS guards
linkedPullRequests.author: Bojun-Feng
linkedPullRequests.body:
#### Why I did it

Fix https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/28125
Fix https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/28127
Fix https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/28130

On most Broadcom Tomahawk-1 platforms (all except Arista 7060CX-32S), syncd crashes at startup with a SIGSEGV when running 202605 ONIE images. Two independent issues prevent bring-up:

1. `one-image.mk` `LAZY_BUILD_INSTALLS` has never included the broadcom-legacy-th kernel module. When the legacy image was first introduced in [#25192](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/25192), `$(BRCM_LEGACY_OPENNSL_KERNEL)` was added to `one-aboot.mk` but never to `one-image.mk`. The subsequent rename in [#26136](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/26136) (`broadcom-legacy` → `broadcom-legacy-th`) naturally couldn't fix what was never there. As a result, ONIE TH1 images declare `broadcom-legacy-th` as a dependent machine but never install its BDE kernel modules, and syncd cannot attach the ASIC.

2. The `SAI_STATS_ST_CAPABILITY_SUPPORTED=0` and `SAI_STATS_EXT_SWITCH_SUPPORTED=0` sai.profile guard (added to Arista 7060CX-32S in PRs [#26201](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/26201) and [#26217](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/26217)) was never propagated to any other TH1 platform. Without it, `HFTelOrch::isSupportedHFTel()` calls `sai_query_stats_st_capability()` which crashes in `brcm_sai_st_pd_ctr_cap_list_get` because TH1's streaming telemetry platform driver is uninitialized.

The sairedis runtime guard mechanism already exists ([sonic-sairedis #1788](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-sairedis/pull/1788)), this PR just adds the missing sai.profile keys to all affected platforms.

#### How I did it

- Added `$(BRCM_LEGACY_TH_OPENNSL_KERNEL)` to `$(SONIC_ONE_IMAGE)_LAZY_BUILD_INSTALLS`, so `one-image.mk` and `one-aboot.mk` are aligned.

- Appended `SAI_STATS_ST_CAPABILITY_SUPPORTED=0` and `SAI_STATS_EXT_SWITCH_SUPPORTED=0` to all 30 TH1 sai.profile/sai.profile.j2 files (Accton, Alpha Networks, Broadcom reference, Celestica, Dell, Delta, Facebook, Ingrasys, Inventec, Juniper, MiTAC, Quanta), mirroring what Arista 7060CX-32S already has.

#### How to verify it

1. Build broadcom-legacy-th ONIE image, `dpkg -l | grep opennsl-modules-legacy-th` should be present
2. Boot on any TH1 platform, syncd logs should show: `disabling query_stats_st_capability for this platform`
3. orchagent logs: `Streaming stats not supported, HFTel disabled` should not result in SIGSEGV

<!--

-->
Fix Tomahawk-1 ONIE image boot failure by adding missing BDE kernel module and SAI_STATS crash guards to all TH1 platforms.
